d1001116-4.desc: Salt pans laid out in a radiating fan pattern, a landmark of the Jiangjun coast when seen from the air.

d1001116-5.name: Jiangjun River Estuary Wetland
d1001116-5.desc: A wetland at the mouth of the Jiangjun River with mangroves and rich migratory birdlife.

d1001110-3.name: Longtian ChaCha Cultural Heritage Park
d1001110-3.desc: A park converted from the warehouses of the Longtian distillery, with interactive exhibits on the Chianan Canal and archaeology.

d1001110-4.name: Hulupi Nature Park
d1001110-4.desc: A pond park in Guantian with a lovers' suspension bridge across the water; also a habitat of the pheasant-tailed jacana.

d1001124-4.name: Yongxing Suspension Bridge
d1001124-4.desc: A long suspension bridge across the Zengwen River with views of the valley and mountains; one of Nanxi's landmarks.

d1001124-5.name: Guidan Hot Spring
d1001124-5.desc: A sodium bicarbonate hot spring in the Nanxi hills with foot baths and a hot spring experience area.

d1001107-4.name: Dianji Theater
d1001107-4.desc: A Japanese-era theater in Madou, now closed, whose Western-style facade still stands on the street.

d1001107-5.name: Madou Huji Temple
d1001107-5.desc: A Mazu temple in the Madou town center, preserving exquisite cut-and-paste ceramic and painted decorations.

d1001107-6.name: Shuikutou Archaeological Park
d1001107-6.desc: The remains of the Qing-era Madou port wharf, preserving relics of the Daofeng Inland Sea period and the legend of the dragon's throat.

d1001112-3.name: Zilongmiao Yongchang Temple
d1001112-3.desc: One of the few temples in Taiwan dedicated to the general Zhao Zilong; the surrounding village is named after it.

d1001112-4.name: Jiali Zhongshan Park
d1001112-4.desc: A green park in the Jiali town center shaded by old trees, where residents stroll and exercise.

d1001119-3.name: Shanhua Brewery
d1001119-3.desc: A Taiwan Tobacco and Liquor Corporation brewery where visitors can tour the production line and taste fresh beer.

d1001119-4.name: Hucuoliao Mural Village
d1001119-4.desc: A mural village that began with a daughter painting for her mother; its walls are covered with fairy-tale and animal scenes.

d1001119-5.name: Qieba Tianhou Temple
d1001119-5.desc: A historic Mazu temple in Qieba, Shanhua, and the center of local faith.

d1001114-4.name: Xigang Granary Restaurant
d1001114-4.desc: A restaurant converted from the Xigang Farmers' Association's old granary, retaining the granary's exterior and interior space.

d1001111-4.name: Toushe Kuwa Shrine
d1001111-4.desc: The ritual house of the Siraya community of Toushe, where a night ceremony honoring the ancestral spirits is held in the tenth lunar month each year.

d1001111-5.name: Danei Bridge
d1001111-5.desc: A large bridge across the Zengwen River, the main gateway into the Danei town center.

d1001115-4.name: Guoshenggang Lighthouse
d1001115-4.desc: A black-and-white steel-frame lighthouse on the sandbar at the westernmost point of Taiwan's main island.

d1001115-5.name: Liukong Pier
d1001115-5.desc: A boat pier on the Qigu Lagoon where visitors board rafts to cruise the lagoon and see oyster racks and sandbars.

d1001115-6.name: Dingshan Birdwatching Pavilion
d1001115-6.desc: A birdwatching pavilion in Dingshan, Qigu, for observing black-faced spoonbills and migratory birds in the abandoned salt-pan wetlands.

d1001123-4.name: White Church (Yintian Shanfang)
d1001123-4.desc: A pure-white Japanese-style chapel inside the Yintian Shanfang garden, a popular wedding-photo spot in Yujing.

d1001123-5.name: Yujing Mango Ice Street
d1001123-5.desc: The streets around Yujing Market, lined with mango shaved-ice shops and busiest in the summer mango season.

d1001121-3.name: Sucuo Zhenhu Temple
d1001121-3.desc: A Wangye temple in Sucuo that, like Changxing Temple, holds a royal-boat festival every three years.

d1001122-3.name: Taiwan Orchid Plantation
d1001122-3.desc: An ecological park themed on Taiwan's native orchids, with orchid greenhouses and landscaped trails.

d1001120-3.name: Yingxi Lake, Southern Taiwan Science Park
d1001120-3.desc: An artificial lake inside the science park; the lakeside path and large art installation are the park's leisure landmark.

d1001120-4.name: Tree Valley Farm
d1001120-4.desc: A family leisure farm in Tree Valley Park where visitors can feed goats, rabbits and other small animals up close.

d1002106-3.name: Taijiang National Park Visitor Center
d1002106-3.desc: A visitor center shaped like a cluster of white stilt houses; the buildings mirrored in the water are a Sicao landmark.

d1002106-4.name: Koxinga Landing Monument at Luermen
d1002106-4.desc: A monument at the mouth of Luermen Creek marking the spot where Koxinga's army landed in Taiwan.

d1002106-5.name: Anshun Salt Field
d1002106-5.desc: Salt pans opened in the Japanese era, now the Salt Field Eco-Culture Village, preserving tile-paved and fan-shaped salt pans.

d1001125-4.name: Beiliao Old Street
d1001125-4.desc: A mountain-village old street near Nanhua Reservoir that keeps its old houses and simple hill-settlement character.

d1001126-4.name: 308 Highland Lookout
d1001126-4.desc: A lookout on a hill about 308 m high, overlooking the Moon World badlands, sunrise and seas of clouds.

d1001118-4.name: Damujiang Cultural Park
d1001118-4.desc: Xinhua was once called Damujiang; the park restores Japanese-era dormitories next to the Butokuden.

d1001118-5.name: Xinhua Chaotian Temple
d1001118-5.desc: A Mazu temple beside Xinhua Old Street and the center of faith for the Xinhua town area.

d1001118-6.name: Guaguayuan Sweet Potato Story House
d1001118-6.desc: A sweet-potato-themed tourist factory introducing Taiwan's sweet potato industry and processing.

d1001131-3.name: Yongkang Erwang Temple
d1001131-3.desc: The main temple of Erwang Village in Yongkang, dedicated to the Second Prince deity and a center of local faith.

d1001131-4.name: Yongkang Adventure Education Park
d1001131-4.desc: A park known for its adventure play equipment, with large slides and climbing structures.

d1002104-3.name: Sanshan Guowang Temple
d1002104-3.desc: Built by Hakka settlers from eastern Guangdong in the Qing era, a rare Chaozhou-style temple and national monument.

d1002104-4.name: Xihua Hall
d1002104-4.desc: A Qing-era vegetarian hall of the Jinchuang sect of Zhaijiao, a rare surviving hall of its kind in the city.

d1002102-5.name: Koxinga Shrine
d1002102-5.desc: A shrine to Koxinga, formerly the Kaishan King Temple, rebuilt as a shrine in the late Qing at Shen Baozhen's petition.

d1002102-6.name: Temple of the Five Concubines
d1002102-6.desc: A temple and tomb honoring the five concubines of Ming Prince Ningjing, a national monument.

d1002102-7.name: Judicial Museum (Former Tainan District Court)
d1002102-7.desc: The Japanese-era Tainan District Court, a Baroque-style building by Moriyama Matsunosuke and a national monument.

d1002102-8.name: Heyue Plaza (The Spring)
d1002102-8.desc: A sunken water plaza built where the China Town mall was demolished, at the canal end of Zhongzheng Road.

d1002102-9.name: Shuixian Temple
d1002102-9.desc: An old temple to the Water Immortals, once the meeting hall of Tainan's three merchant guilds, now inside Yongle Market.

d1002102-10.name: Beiji Temple
d1002102-10.desc: A Ming-Zheng-era temple to Xuantian Shangdi with a plaque inscribed by Prince Ningjing, a national monument.

d1002102-11.name: Wind God Temple
d1002102-11.desc: Taiwan's only temple dedicated to the Wind God, with a Qing-era stone archway of the official reception pavilion in front.

d1002102-12.name: Wu Garden
d1002102-12.desc: A garden built by Qing-era merchant Wu Shangxin, one of Taiwan's four famous gardens, next to the Public Hall.

d1002107-4.name: Yuguang Island
d1002107-4.desc: A sandbar island off Anping; the Crescent Bay beach and windbreak forest are a favorite sunset spot.

d1002107-5.name: Blessing of the Big Fish
d1002107-5.desc: A large whale-shaped public artwork in Harbor History Park; visitors can walk inside to view the canal.

d1002107-6.name: Haishan Hall
d1002107-6.desc: The Qing-era guild hall of the Haishan naval battalion, a Fujian-style house now serving as Anping's folk culture exhibition hall.

d1002107-7.name: Anping Dingqing Pier
d1002107-7.desc: A waterfront pier park on Anping Harbor beside the Te Yang destroyer, a place to watch the harbor and sunset.

d1002101-4.name: Magistrate's Residence
d1002101-4.desc: The Japanese-era residence of the Tainan prefectural governor, a red-brick mansion that once hosted Japanese royalty.

d1002101-5.name: Tainan Station Historic Building
d1002101-5.desc: The Japanese-era station building, a national monument whose second floor once housed the Railway Hotel.

d1001129-3.name: Qianfoshan Puti Temple
d1001129-3.desc: A large Buddhist monastery in the Guanmiao hills, founded by Master Baiyun.

d1001129-4.name: Guanmiao Transfer Station
d1001129-4.desc: A Greater Tainan bus transfer station, the hub for routes to Longqi, Xinhua and downtown.

d1002103-4.name: Xishu Old Street
d1002103-4.desc: An old coastal settlement in South District, known in recent years for community art and restored old houses.

d1002103-5.name: Wanli Wannian Temple
d1002103-5.desc: The Wangye temple of Wanli, which keeps a royal boat inside and serves as the area's center of faith.

d1002103-6.name: Shuipingwen Park
d1002103-6.desc: A large green park in the city with lawns, a pond and sports facilities.

d1001127-3.name: Erkong New Village Military Dependents' Culture Park
d1001127-3.desc: An air force dependents' village in Rende, part of which has been preserved and turned into a culture park.

d1001128-4.name: Asia-Pacific International Baseball Training Center
d1001128-4.desc: A national-level baseball training base in Shalun with a main stadium plus youth and little-league fields.

d1001128-5.name: Dunyuan Confucius Temple
d1001128-5.desc: Guiren's Confucius temple, built by local gentry, which holds a Confucius memorial ceremony every year.

d1001128-6.name: Qijia Flower Park
d1001128-6.desc: A flower-growing zone in Qijia, Guiren, mainly orchid and potted-plant nurseries open for visits and purchases.

d1001128-7.name: Shalun Green Energy Science City
d1001128-7.desc: A green-energy R&D cluster next to THSR Tainan Station, home to a green technology demonstration site.

d1001103-6.name: Baihe Reservoir
d1001103-6.desc: A multipurpose reservoir opened in 1965 at the foot of Guanziling, long troubled by heavy siltation.
facts: Opened 1965 for irrigation, flood control and water supply
Concrete-core rolled earthfill dam, 42.5 m high
Severe siltation; ongoing dredging to restore capacity

d1001125-5.name: Jingmian Reservoir
d1001125-5.desc: A small reservoir in Nanhua District, completed in 1980 and now a backup source for Nanhua Reservoir.
facts: Smallest of the seven reservoirs in Siraya National Scenic Area
Built for mango-orchard irrigation, later used for public water supply

d1002102-13.name: National University of Tainan
d1002102-13.desc: Traces its history to the 1899 Tainan Normal School and became a comprehensive university in 2004; the Red House is a Japanese-era school building.
facts: 33 Shulin St. Sec. 2, West Central District

d1001128-8.name: Chang Jung Christian University
d1001128-8.desc: Founded in 1993 as Chang Jung College of Management and upgraded to a university in 2002; Presbyterian-affiliated.

d1001131-5.name: Southern Taiwan University of Science and Technology
d1001131-5.desc: A private university of science and technology in Yongkang District; motto 'Faith, Righteousness, Sincerity, Honesty'.
facts: Private university of science and technology

d1001131-6.name: Kun Shan University
d1001131-6.desc: Founded as Kun Shan Junior College of Technology in 1964 and upgraded in 2000; four colleges.
facts: Private university of science and technology

d1001127-4.name: Chia Nan University of Pharmacy and Science
d1001127-4.desc: Founded in 1966 as Chia Nan Junior College of Pharmacy; one of nine institutions in Taiwan with a pharmacy department.
facts: Private university of science and technology

d1001127-5.name: Chung Hwa University of Medical Technology
d1001127-5.desc: Founded in 1968 and renamed in 2007; focuses on medical professions.
facts: Private university of science and technology

d1001120-5.name: CTBC University of Technology
d1001120-5.desc: Formerly Far East University; renamed in August 2024 after funding from CTBC Bank.
facts: Private university of science and technology

d1002106-6.name: CTBC Business School
d1002106-6.desc: Founded in 2000 as Hsing Kuo University of Management; renamed in 2015 after funding from CTBC Financial Holding.

d1002101-6.name: Tainan Theological College and Seminary
d1002101-6.desc: A Presbyterian Church in Taiwan seminary tracing back to an 1869 preacher-training class (not in the MOE higher-education list).

chihkan.name: Chihkan Tower
chihkan.desc: The site of Fort Provintia, built by the Dutch in 1652; one of Tainan's most representative monuments, lit in yellow at night.

anping-fort.name: Anping Old Fort
anping-fort.desc: Fort Zeelandia, built from 1624, the hub of Dutch rule over Taiwan; a national monument.

anping-treehouse.name: Anping Tree House
anping-treehouse.desc: A former Tait & Co. warehouse overgrown by banyan trees, next to Anping Old Fort.

eternal-fort.name: Eternal Golden Castle
eternal-fort.desc: A Western-style fort planned by Shen Baozhen in 1874, Taiwan's first modern gun battery.

confucius.name: Tainan Confucius Temple
confucius.desc: Founded in 1665 as Taiwan's first academy, the island's first Confucius temple.

hayashi.name: Hayashi Department Store
hayashi.desc: A Japanese-era department store opened in 1932, preserving its cage elevator and rooftop shrine.

shennong.name: Shennong Street
shennong.desc: An old street of the Qing-era Five Canals district, preserving long narrow shophouses and lantern-lit nights.

blueprint.name: Blueprint Culture and Creative Park
blueprint.desc: A creative park converted from former judicial dormitories, famous for its 3D blueprint in blue and white lines.

chimei.name: Chimei Museum
chimei.desc: A white museum designed by Shigeru Ban, housing Western art, musical instruments and arms.

tendrum.name: Ten Drum Rende Sugar Factory Cultural Park
tendrum.desc: A drum-arts creative park converted from the Rende Sugar Factory, keeping its chimney and workshops.

nmth.name: National Museum of Taiwan History
nmth.desc: A national museum themed on four hundred years of Taiwan's history.

sicao.name: Sicao Green Tunnel
sicao.desc: A mangrove waterway in Taijiang National Park, traversed by bamboo raft.

qigu-salt.name: Qigu Salt Mountain
qigu-salt.desc: A white mountain of piled sun-dried salt that you can climb, with salty popsicles and salt sculpture activities.

jingzaijiao.name: Jingzaijiao Tile-paved Salt Fields
jingzaijiao.desc: Taiwan's oldest surviving tile-paved salt fields, famous for their sunset reflections.

nankunshen.name: Nankunshen Daitian Temple
nankunshen.desc: The head temple of Wangye worship in Taiwan, a national monument.

madou-temple.name: Madou Daitian Temple
madou-temple.desc: A Five Wangye temple famous for its giant dragon with heaven and hell scenes.

soulangh.name: Soulangh Cultural Park
soulangh.desc: An arts park converted from the Jiali Sugar Factory, with a children's art museum and exhibitions.

wushantou.name: Wushantou Reservoir
wushantou.desc: The water source of the Chianan Irrigation Canal designed by Yoichi Hatta; the Coral Lake scenic area.

guanziling.name: Guanziling Hot Spring
guanziling.desc: A rare mud hot spring, one of Taiwan's four great hot springs.

hutoupi.name: Hutoupi Scenic Area
hutoupi.desc: Taiwan's first reservoir, with a lakeside trail and suspension bridge.

qingan.name: Xigang Qing'an Temple
qingan.desc: Dedicated to the Qiansui Wangye; the triennial 'Xigang Pilgrimage' has been run by Qing'an Temple since 1823, covering nearly a hundred villages, and is a nationally important folk custom.

zizhu.name: Nanhua Zizhu Temple
zizhu.desc: A Guanyin temple in the Nanhua hills facing the Chianan Plain with mountain views; the farm produce collection yard at its entrance makes it a gathering place for hikers.

jintang.name: Jiali Jintang Temple
jintang.desc: Dedicated to the Zhu, Lei and Yin Qiansui; the triennial 'Soulangh Pilgrimage' is one of Tainan's five great pilgrimages, famous for its Centipede Formation.

nm-garden.name: Garden Night Market
nm-garden.desc: One of Tainan's three big night markets, open Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

nm-dadong.name: Dadong Night Market
nm-dadong.desc: Open Monday, Tuesday and Friday; since 2023 split into two adjacent sections, Dadong and Dadong East.

nm-wusheng.name: Wusheng Night Market
nm-wusheng.desc: Open Wednesday and Saturday (single source, worth re-checking).

nm-xiaobei.name: Xiaobei Chenggong Night Market
nm-xiaobei.desc: Section 4, Ximen Road, North District; Tuesday and Friday, 17:00 to 00:00.

nm-fuguo.name: Yongkang Fuguo Night Market
nm-fuguo.desc: Fuguo 1st Road, Yongkang District; recorded as open Tuesday and Friday, to be confirmed.

nm-xinying.name: Xinying Night Market
nm-xinying.desc: The largest night market north of the Zengwen River; recorded as open Monday and Thursday, to be confirmed.

stsp-admin.name: STSP Administration Bureau
stsp-admin.desc: The Tainan Science Park of the Southern Taiwan Science Park sits at the junction of Sinshih, Shanhua and Anding; phases 1 and 2 cover about 1,043 hectares.

stsp-fab.name: Wafer Fab Area (TSMC)
stsp-fab.desc: TSMC is the park's main tenant; in 2017 it announced fabs for its advanced 5 nm and 3 nm processes in the Tainan park.

stsp-rd.name: R&D and Incubation Area
stsp-rd.desc: Research institutions and start-up incubation space on the park's east side; phase 3 expands onto Taiwan Sugar land in Sinshih District.

stsp-life.name: Park Living Area
stsp-life.desc: The residential and amenity area around the staff dormitories, shopping mall and Tree Valley Park.

beehive.name: Yanshui Beehive Fireworks
beehive.when: Lantern Festival, the 15th day of the 1st lunar month, every year
beehive.desc: Originating from a late-Qing plague custom of inviting Guan Yu on procession while setting off firecrackers along the way; now famous for fireworks 'castles' launching hundreds of thousands of rockets at once, one of Taiwan's most iconic Lantern Festival events.

wangchuan.name: Xigang Pilgrimage · Burning of the Royal Boat
wangchuan.when: Once every three years (Ox, Dragon, Goat and Dog years), 4th lunar month
wangchuan.desc: The Xigang Pilgrimage has been run by Qing'an Temple since 1823; its procession covers nearly a hundred villages and is a nationally important folk custom. On the final day the royal boat is burned to send off the Qiansui Wangye and the boat, symbolically carrying the plague away.

centipede.name: Soulangh Pilgrimage · Centipede Formation
centipede.when: Once every three years; 2026 is a pilgrimage year
centipede.desc: The Soulangh Pilgrimage of Jiali Jintang Temple is one of Tainan's five great pilgrimages. In the Centipede Formation, children dressed as deity generals ride a long row of platforms through the procession; in 2026 its 108 sections were certified by Guinness World Records.

yuejin.name: Yuejin Lantern Festival
yuejin.when: About a month around Lunar New Year each year (centered on the Lantern Festival)
yuejin.desc: A light-art festival on the water of Yuejin Harbor in Yanshui, in its 15th year in 2025 and extended to Xinying since 2024.

dongshan.name: Dongshan Welcoming the Buddha
dongshan.when: Escorted to Biyun Temple on the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, and back to Bixuan Temple on the 10th day of the 1st lunar month
dongshan.desc: A round-trip procession of the Guanyin Buddha between Bixuan Temple in Dongshan and Biyun Temple in Baihe, a nationally important folk custom; devotees escort the palanquin on foot over mountain roads.

xuejia.name: Xuejia Shang Baijiao Pilgrimage
xuejia.when: Around the 11th day of the 3rd lunar month
xuejia.desc: The ancestral rite of Xuejia Ciji Temple, paying homage from afar to the ancestral temple in Baijiao, Fujian, with a Centipede Formation and procession troupes.

longqi.name: Longci Light Festival · Empty Mountain Festival
longqi.when: About a month around Lunar New Year
longqi.desc: A forest lantern festival in Huxing Mountain Park, hailed as the most beautiful mountain lantern festival in the country.

kapok.name: Baihe Kapok Blossom Season
kapok.desc: The kapok avenue at Linchupi comes into full bloom, painting the whole of Baihe orange-red.

jiangjun.name: Jiangjun Roar Music Festival
jiangjun.when: Every summer (around the first weekend of July)
jiangjun.desc: A beach music festival on Mashagou beach, with stage lights and crowds at night.

anping-ny.name: Anping New Year's Eve Fireworks and Spring Welcome
anping-ny.when: New Year's Eve on 31 December, and the 1st day of the 1st lunar month
anping-ny.desc: New Year's Eve fireworks and Lunar New Year celebrations in front of Anping Kaitai Tianhou Temple.

luermen.name: Luermen Shengmu Temple Spring Fireworks
luermen.when: Around the 1st day of the 1st lunar month
luermen.desc: The Orthodox Luermen Shengmu Temple is famous for welcoming the new year with high-altitude fireworks, the largest display in Tainan.

lotus.name: Baihe Lotus Festival
lotus.desc: Baihe's lotus fields in full bloom; the Lotus Park and lotus-viewing trails are the main spots.

cypress.name: Liujia Bald Cypress Season
cypress.desc: The bald cypresses along Jingpupi turn orange-red, giving all of Liujia its autumn colors.

plum.name: Meiling Plum Blossom Viewing
plum.desc: Meiling's plum trees bloom in January, turning the Nanxi hills into a sea of white blossoms.

firefly.name: Meiling Firefly Season
firefly.desc: Swarms of fireflies at night along the Meiling trails, Tainan's best-known firefly-watching spot.

spoonbill.name: Black-faced Spoonbill Season
spoonbill.desc: Black-faced spoonbills winter in Qigu Lagoon and the Zengwen River estuary, the world's most important wintering site.

caltrop.name: Guantian Water Caltrop Season
caltrop.desc: Harvest season for Guantian's water caltrops; the caltrop fields are breeding habitat for the pheasant-tailed jacana.

madou.name: Madou Pilgrimage (Five Wangye Pilgrimage)
madou.when: Once every three years (same year as the Xigang Pilgrimage), 3rd lunar month
madou.desc: The pilgrimage procession of the Five Wangye of Madou Daitian Temple, one of Nanying's five great pilgrimages.

tucheng.name: Tucheng Pilgrimage
tucheng.when: Once every three years (Ox, Dragon, Goat and Dog years), 3rd lunar month
tucheng.desc: The pilgrimage procession of the Orthodox Luermen Shengmu Temple, one of Nanying's five great pilgrimages, with a Centipede Formation and procession troupes.

shibayao.name: Sinhua Shibayao
shibayao.desc: A night procession of Sinhua Wu'an Temple after the Lantern Festival, said to drive away a spider demon, with firecrackers going off all along the streets.

sixteen.name: Tainan Turning Sixteen
sixteen.when: Qixi (7th day of the 7th lunar month)
sixteen.desc: A coming-of-age rite on the Seven Maidens' birthday at Kailong Temple, where sixteen-year-olds crawl under the Qiniangma pavilion; a custom unique to Tainan.

orchid.name: Taiwan International Orchid Show
orchid.desc: The international orchid show at Wushulin in Houbi, one of the world's three great orchid shows.

hotspringfair.name: Guanziling Hot Spring Food Festival
hotspringfair.when: Late September to October every year
hotspringfair.desc: A food market and hot-spring experience opening the Guanziling mud hot spring season.

siraya.name: Toushe Siraya Night Ceremony
siraya.desc: The Siraya people of Toushe in Danei honour their ancestral spirit Alid at night: a bonfire is lit before the kuwa shrine, offerings are made and the hand-in-hand round dance and songs go on until dawn. A registered folk-culture asset of Tainan City.
siraya.when: Nights of the 14th and 15th days of the 10th lunar month

confucius.name: Confucius Temple Ceremony
confucius.when: Early morning of September 28 (Teachers' Day) every year
confucius.desc: The autumn sacrificial rite at Tainan Confucius Temple, Taiwan's first school. Officiants perform the three offerings in ancient form, students in period robes perform the Eight-Row Dance, and afterwards people pluck the ox's "wisdom hairs".

mazu.name: Grand Matsu Temple: Mazu's Birthday
mazu.when: Around Mazu's birthday on the 23rd day of the 3rd lunar month
mazu.desc: The Grand Matsu Temple was Taiwan's first state-built Mazu temple. Around her birthday there are celebration rites and a pilgrimage, with devotees walking from the old city to Anping.

dragonboat.name: Tainan International Dragon Boat Championships
dragonboat.when: About five days around the Dragon Boat Festival, on the Tainan Canal between Anyi and Chengtian bridges
dragonboat.desc: Every Dragon Boat Festival, international and local teams race on the Tainan Canal while crowds cheer from the banks. It ran May 27–31 in 2025 and June 17–21 in 2026.

mango.name: Tainan International Mango Festival (Yujing)
mango.when: Late June to July every year (based on past years; check the official announcement)
mango.desc: A harvest festival for mango season, with markets, tastings and mango shaved ice rotating through Yujing, Nanxi, Nanhua and Zuozhen. Yujing is the home of Taiwan's Irwin mangoes.

pomelo.name: Madou Pomelo Festival
pomelo.when: About a month before Mid-Autumn Festival (pomelo harvest; dates based on past years, unverified)
pomelo.desc: Madou wentan pomelos are harvested around White Dew, and markets and promotions are held in the growing area before Mid-Autumn Festival.

pineapple.name: Tainan Pineapple and Bamboo Shoot Season (Guanmiao)
pineapple.when: May to June, during pineapple and bamboo shoot season (dates based on past years, unverified)
pineapple.desc: A promotion for Guanmiao's pineapples and bamboo shoots, once held at Shanxi Temple with games, crafts and a cooking contest.

rice.name: Tainan Good Rice Festival (Jingliao, Houbi)
rice.when: October every year (from October 9 in 2026); the painted rice field is planted in August
rice.desc: A rice festival run by the Houbi farmers' association. The Jingliao fields grow a painted rice field, and the autumn harvest brings rice-cutting, rice dishes and an old-street market. Houbi is the setting of the documentary Let It Be.

coffee.name: Dongshan Coffee Festival
coffee.when: From around October to November (based on past years; check the official announcement)
coffee.desc: Dongshan's coffee harvest season. Tainan has held a specialty coffee competition since 2013, followed each autumn by a coffee festival along the Dongshan Coffee Road.

flametree.name: Flame Tree Season
flametree.desc: Tainan is called the Phoenix City; the flame trees on the NCKU campus and across the city burst into red blossoms during graduation season.

roleDescriptions.student: Takes the shuttle bus between the transit hub and campus every day, and often stays at the library or gym after school.
roleDescriptions.commuter: Lives in social housing, a ten-minute walk from the transit hub, and likes to stroll along the waterfront at lunch.
roleDescriptions.nurse: Works shifts between the community clinic and the day-care center, and makes regular home visits to seniors.
roleDescriptions.researcher: Works in the open lab, regularly runs science camps on campus, and often visits the bookstore.
roleDescriptions.artist: A resident member of the black-box theater, performing outdoors at the waterfront pavilion on weekends.
roleDescriptions.elder: Spends the day at the day-care center and walks to the green island every day on the doctor's walking prescription.
roleDescriptions.family: Drops the kids at the nursery in the morning; on weekends the whole family walks to the memory hall for exhibitions.
roleDescriptions.child: Runs and plays at the inclusive playground and the plaza after school, and goes out and about with the family on holidays.

dayCycle.note: The city is resting; only night shifts and a few pedestrians remain.

dayCycle.label: Early morning
dayCycle.note: The sky brightens; the fishing villages of Qigu and Beimen wake first.

dayCycle.label: Rush hour
dayCycle.note: The flows from Yongkang and Rende into the city center are at their busiest.

dayCycle.label: Daytime
dayCycle.note: Farms, the science park and campuses each go about their business.

dayCycle.label: Dusk
dayCycle.note: Work and school let out; crowds head for residential areas and night markets.

dayCycle.label: Night
dayCycle.note: Windows light up, and people are still strolling along the canal.

city.name: City Tour
city.blurb: A minute or so around Tainan: stations, monuments, the science park, salt fields and hot springs.
captions: Welcome to HEX CITY Tainan. The islands are the real outlines of the 37 districts; the next minute or so takes you around the city.
Tainan Station: the special-class station on the Western Trunk Line. Trains run from Houbi to Shalun, stopping at every station and turning back at the end.
Chihkan Tower: Fort Provintia, built by the Dutch in 1653, the starting point of Tainan's four hundred years of history.
Anping Old Fort: the site of Fort Zeelandia, Taiwan's earliest Western-style castle, facing the former Taijiang Inland Sea.
Southern Taiwan Science Park: the fence encloses the administration bureau, wafer fabs and R&D area; the daytime commuters all head here.
Yanshui Beehive Fireworks: on Lantern Festival night tens of thousands of rockets fire at once in front of Wu Temple, and the fireworks grow denser as night falls.
Qigu Salt Mountain: the salt fields and salt mountain of the west coast, at their best in the sunset glow.
Guanziling Hot Spring: a rare mud hot spring at the foot of the Baihe hills, with the morning mountain mist not yet lifted.
Shalun Station: the terminus of the Shalun Line and also HSR Tainan Station, where the trains turn back.
End of the tour. Click any district, building, station or pedestrian on the road to keep exploring Tainan.

temples.name: Temple Tour
temples.blurb: From the official temples of the old city to the Wangye temples by the sea: a map of Tainan's faith.
captions: Tainan has the highest density of temples in Taiwan. This trip starts from the official temples of the old city and heads north to the Wangye temples by the sea.
Sacrificial Rites Martial Temple: the Guan Yu temple of official Qing-era worship and a national monument; its red wall along Yongfu Road is the most famous wall in the old city.
Grand Matsu Temple: a Mazu temple converted from the mansion of the Ming Prince of Ningjing, the first officially built Mazu temple in Taiwan.
Tainan Confucius Temple: Taiwan's first academy, built in 1665, with red walls, old trees and the Dacheng Hall.
Anping Kaitai Tianhou Temple: the Mazu temple of the people of Anping, with Anping Old Street right in front.
Orthodox Luermen Shengmu Temple: said to be the largest temple complex in Taiwan; the New Year spring fireworks are launched here.
Xigang Qing'an Temple: the triennial Xigang Pilgrimage sets out from here and ends with the burning of the royal boat to send off the gods.
Madou Daitian Temple: the great temple of the Five Wangye; the Eighteen Hells and giant dragon behind it are a childhood memory for many.
Xuejia Ciji Temple: a Baosheng Dadi temple; every year the Shang Baijiao rite returns to the bank of the Jiangjun River, where Koxinga landed, to honor the ancestral temple from afar.
Nankunshen Daitian Temple: the head temple of Wangye worship in Taiwan, with pilgrim groups arriving all year round.
Nanhua Zizhu Temple: a Guanyin sanctuary in the hills; we have come all the way from the coast into the mountains.
End of the temple tour. Open "Events" to see what temple festivals like the beehive fireworks, royal boat burning and Centipede Formation look like.

heritage.name: A Day of Monuments
heritage.blurb: Dutch, Ming Zheng, Qing and Japanese eras: four hundred years in one day.
captions: Tainan's four hundred years of history lie layered through the city. This trip goes in chronological order: Dutch, Ming Zheng, Qing, Japanese.
Anping Old Fort: Fort Zeelandia, built by the Dutch in 1624, the opening scene of Taiwan's history.
Chihkan Tower: Fort Provintia of 1653; after retaking Taiwan, Koxinga set up the Chengtian Prefecture here.
Jiali Yanping Junwang Temple: commemorates Koxinga; the Jiali area was an important base of Ming Zheng settlement.
Great East Gate: the east gate of the Qing-era Taiwan prefectural city; the walls are gone, but the gate still stands in the middle of the roundabout.
Eternal Golden Castle: a Western-style fort built in 1874 by Shen Baozhen with French engineers, in response to the Mudan Incident.
Hayashi Department Store: a Japanese-era department store opened in 1932, with the only elevator in southern Taiwan at the time.
National Museum of Taiwan Literature: the former Tainan Prefecture Hall, a government building with a Mansard roof completed in 1916.
Sinhua Butokuden: a Japanese-era martial arts hall, with the old street right next door.
Yoichi Hatta Memorial Park: the designer of Wushantou Reservoir and the Chianan Irrigation Canal; the dormitory cluster has been preserved.
Jingliao Holy Cross Church: a pyramid church designed in 1960 by Pritzker Prize winner Gottfried Böhm, modern architecture amid the rice paddies.
End of the day of monuments. Every building's card has a Google Maps link, so you can plan a route directly.

night.name: Night Market Night
night.blurb: Follow the crowds after dark through six night markets and see which days they open.
captions: Tainan's night markets are not open every day; locals remember it as 'Da-Da-Wu-Hua-Da-Wu-Hua'. This trip runs from dusk to late night.
Garden Night Market: open Thursday, Saturday and Sunday; the big night market of the North District, with crowds streaming in from all directions after dark.
Dadong Night Market: open Monday, Tuesday and Friday; in the East District near NCKU, with the most students.
Wusheng Night Market: open Wednesday and Saturday; a long-established night market in the West Central District.
Xiaobei Chenggong Night Market: open Tuesday and Friday; another option in the North District.
Yongkang Fuguo Night Market: the night market of Yongkang locals, not far from the city center.
Xinying Night Market: the largest night market north of the Zengwen River, a short walk from Xinying Station.
Shennong Street: after the night market, stroll the old street, where the Qing-era Five Canals left behind their shophouses.
End of night market night. Drag the timeline to the evening and the pedestrians will head on their own to whichever night market is open today.

mountainsea.name: Mountains and Sea
mountainsea.blurb: From the lagoons and salt fields of the west coast to the reservoirs, Meiling and Moon World in the east.
captions: West of Tainan are lagoons and salt fields; to the east, foothills and reservoirs. This trip goes from dawn at the coast to dusk in the mountains.
Qigu Lagoon: Taiwan's largest lagoon, with oyster racks and rafts; the fishermen head out first at dawn.
Jingzaijiao Tile-paved Salt Fields: the oldest surviving tile-paved salt fields, most famous for their sunset reflections.
Black-faced Spoonbill Ecology Exhibition Hall: from October to March each year, black-faced spoonbills come to the Zengwen River estuary to winter.
Sicao Green Tunnel: a waterway hemmed in by mangroves, with rafts drifting slowly through.
Wushantou Reservoir: completed in 1930; the name Coral Lake comes from the coral-like shoreline seen from the air.
Zengwen Reservoir: Taiwan's largest reservoir, supplying irrigation and domestic water to the Chianan Plain.
Meiling Scenic Area: plum blossoms in winter and fireflies in late spring, up in the Nanxi hills.
Caoshan Moon World: mudstone badlands, grey-white ridges where nothing grows.
Erliao Sunrise Pavilion: a famous low-altitude sunrise spot, where seas of clouds rise from the valleys of Moon World.
Guanziling Hot Spring: mud hot springs at dusk, where the mountains-and-sea day comes to a close.
End of the mountains and sea day. On the mountain trails and cycle paths you can also see riders going back and forth on the map.

flows.F1: School run: students from Nanxi District go to class in Nanhua District.
flows.F2: Commute: office workers who live in Qigu District and work in Annan District.
flows.F3: Walking prescription: seniors from Baihe District walk to Dongshan District.
flows.F4: Collaboration: researchers from Yujing District run science camps in Zuojhen District.
flows.F5: Performance: artists from Guantian District perform in Danei District.
flows.F6: Family day: families from Liuying District visit the market in Liujia District.
flows.F7: Home care: caregivers from Sinhua District visit seniors in Longci District.

dan-zai-noodles.name: Danzai Noodles
dan-zai-noodles.desc: Tan-tsai noodles began around 1895 when fisherman Hong Yu-tou sold noodles from a shoulder pole outside Shuixian Temple during typhoon season.

coffin-bread.name: Coffin Bread
coffin-bread.desc: Deep-fried thick toast hollowed out and filled with creamy chowder, created at a Sakariba (now Kangle Market) food stall in the Japanese era.

shrimp-rice.name: Shrimp Rice
shrimp-rice.desc: Local huoshao shrimp stir-fried with soy sauce and sugar, then steamed into rice with its sauce; several old shops line Hai'an Road.

shrimp-roll.name: Shrimp Roll
shrimp-roll.desc: Huoshao shrimp, minced pork, celery and fish paste wrapped in caul fat and deep-fried; a signature snack around Anping Old Street.

anping-douhua.name: Anping Douhua
anping-douhua.desc: Silky tofu pudding in syrup with toppings like tapioca or red beans, a popular dessert near Anping Fort.

milkfish-skin-soup.name: Milkfish Skin Soup
milkfish-skin-soup.desc: Milkfish shops on Kaiyuan Road prepare fish each dawn; skin or belly soup with braised-pork rice is a classic Tainan breakfast.

xishu-flour-cake.name: Xishu Flour Pastry
xishu-flour-cake.desc: A traditional Xishu pastry, named with Kunshen oyster fritters and Wanli lizardfish balls as the 'three crisps' of Kun-Xi-Wan.

mango-shaved-ice.name: Mango Shaved Ice
mango-shaved-ice.desc: Yujing is a key Irwin mango area; in summer old-street shops pile fresh mango on shaved ice, with district-run mango-ice tours.

madou-wagui.name: Wa-guei Rice Pudding
madou-wagui.desc: Steamed rice-batter bowls with braised pork and egg yolk; Madou has third-generation shops dating back to Japanese-era peddlers.

madou-pomelo.name: Madou Pomelo
madou-pomelo.desc: Juicy, sweet-tart Madou pomelos were a Qing-era tribute fruit and are harvested around the White Dew solar term.

water-caltrop-fritter.name: Water Caltrop Fritters
water-caltrop-fritter.desc: Guantian is called the home of red water caltrops; in autumn the nuts are battered and fried into a popular snack.

yanshui-yi-mein.name: Yanshui Yi Noodles
yanshui-yi-mein.desc: Flat egg noodles kneaded with duck egg and sun-dried, tossed with meat sauce and sprouts; Yanshui's signature snack.

xiaying-goose.name: Goose Meat
xiaying-goose.desc: Xiaying is Tainan's goose-farming hometown; white goose is one of its three treasures with black beans and silk.

shanhua-beef-soup.name: Beef Soup
shanhua-beef-soup.desc: Shanhua's large cattle slaughterhouse sends fresh beef to soup shops by dawn, underpinning Tainan's beef-soup culture.

guanmiao-noodles.name: Guanmiao Noodles
guanmiao-noodles.desc: Dating to the Japanese era, hand-folded noodles are sun-dried on bamboo trays for days and keep without preservatives.

lotus-seed.name: Lotus Seeds
lotus-seed.desc: Baihe grows about two-thirds of Taiwan's lotus seeds; the lotus festival brings lotus-seed ice, cakes and lotus banquets.

urn-roasted-chicken.name: Urn-Roasted Chicken
urn-roasted-chicken.desc: A Guanziling hot-spring specialty: whole chickens hung in clay urns and roasted over longan wood until golden and crisp.

meiling-plum.name: Meiling Plums
meiling-plum.desc: Meiling has over 300 ha of plum trees; spring green plums become crisp pickled plums, shiso plums and plum chicken soup.

dongshan-coffee.name: Dongshan Coffee
dongshan-coffee.desc: Coffee is grown along the hills of Route 175 in Dongshan, often shaded under longan trees.

dried-longan.name: Wood-Smoked Dried Longan
dried-longan.desc: Dongshan is Taiwan's main longan area; fruit is traditionally smoke-dried for days in wood-fired earthen kilns.

milkfish-congee.name: Milkfish Congee
milkfish-congee.desc: Xuejia is a milkfish-farming hub; its old congee shops use fish-bone broth with boneless milkfish.

salt-baked-egg.name: Salt-Baked Egg
salt-baked-egg.desc: A snack around the Jingzaijiao tile-paved salt pans: eggs baked in local sea salt.

dried-mango.name: Dried Mango
dried-mango.desc: Nanhua grows Irwin mangoes; farmers hand-make lower-grade fruit into dried mango, now a local specialty.

danei-avocado.name: Avocado
danei-avocado.desc: Danei is Taiwan's largest avocado-growing area; the season runs June to February, peaking in July and August.

green-bamboo-shoot.name: Green Bamboo Shoots
green-bamboo-shoot.desc: Longqi is a main green bamboo shoot area; its sandy soil yields sweet shoots, often eaten chilled in summer.

xinhua-sweet-potato.name: Sweet Potato
xinhua-sweet-potato.desc: Sweet potato is Xinhua's specialty; it was once Taiwan's top sweet-potato starch producer and is credited with chilled roast sweet potatoes.

jingliao-rice.name: Jingliao Rice
jingliao-rice.desc: Houbi rice is nationally known; the documentary 'Let It Be' follows Jingliao farmers, and the old street serves champion rice.

liuying-milk.name: Liuying Fresh Milk
liuying-milk.desc: Liuying is one of Taiwan's four major dairy zones, farming dairy cattle since around 1970.

sesame-oil-chicken.name: Sesame Oil Chicken
sesame-oil-chicken.desc: Xigang is a main sesame-growing area; chicken cooked with local sesame oil and ginger is served dry or as soup.

anding-sesame-oil.name: Sesame Oil
anding-sesame-oil.desc: Anding, with Xigang and Shanhua, forms Tainan's sesame belt; the local farmers' association cold-presses sesame oil.

qigu-oyster.name: Grilled Oysters
qigu-oyster.desc: Oyster racks fill Qigu Lagoon; lagoon boat tours often include freshly grilled plump oysters.

jiangjun-carrot.name: Carrots
jiangjun-carrot.desc: Jiangjun's sandy coastal soil grows sweet carrots; with Jiali it supplies about 70% of Taiwan's crop, harvested March to April.

xinshi-edamame.name: Edamame
xinshi-edamame.desc: Xinshi is known as the home of edamame, grown under contract in spring and autumn and mostly exported to Japan.

douchai-noodles.name: Bean Sprout Noodles
douchai-noodles.desc: An old-style noodle dish of the Chiayi–Tainan border: noodles with bean sprouts and sauce, sold from dawn in Liujia.

cordia-pickle.name: Pickled Cordia
cordia-pickle.desc: On Zuozhen's poor chalky soil, drought-hardy cordia thrives; picked in July, it is boiled and preserved in brine.
